text:
mike: heads up — observed a ~3x reconnect spike and duplicate token billing for some streaming clients after yesterday's taproot routing rollout. telemetry shows lots of short-lived resume attempts.

alexa: oh no. any pattern on region or model?

mike: mostly EU edge nodes, clients on mobile SDKs. route logs show rapid session rebinds: 'resume_id not found -> treat as new' then billing increments twice.

jen: can you paste the minimal trace?

mike: pasted snippet: ```
TRACE route=eu-west-1 taproot=enabled session=abc123 event=resume_attempt status=404
TRACE route=eu-west-1 taproot=enabled session=abc123 event=new_connection billing_increment=1
TRACE route=eu-west-1 taproot=enabled session=abc123 event=resume_attempt status=200 billing_increment=1
```

ryan: that ordering looks like resume requests arriving before the proxy committed the sticky lease. proxy returns 404 -> client reconnects with new session -> gets billed -> resume later succeeds and bills again.

sam: are clients using exponential backoff? mobile SDK still uses a naive tight retry loop for resume.

mike: yes a lot of short windows <200ms between attempts. but even with client backoff we'd still want server-side idempotency for billing.

jen: agree. short-term mitigation options: 1) mark resume-success billing-only if last_event_id matches, 2) add a quick debounce window at billing layer to coalesce dual increments for same logical session, 3) rollback taproot routing for streaming.

alexa: console/alerts — we need a dashboard to show "resume vs new" billing deltas per route so SRE and billing can triage. right now we only show total increments.

console-team: we can add a per-route tag filter: resume_flag=true/false on billing events and expose a chart. can do a quick slice in the next deploy window (2h).

ops-bot: Incident detected: streaming_reconnect_spike (severity: P2). Playbook: investigate->mitigate->deploy fix.

ryan: for a quick patch at ingress: when we see a resume attempt within X ms of a new connection for same client_id, hold billing for Y ms to let resume complete. risk: could underbill if resume never completes.

sam: what if we instead require the resume token be signed and include a monotonic nonce so we can deterministically dedupe billing events? that requires client SDK update. longer path.

mike: immediate plan I'd propose: 1) flip taproot routing for streaming on eu-* back to legacy (rollback) — reduces race surface. 2) server-side debounce in billing for 500ms for same resume_id/session_id marked by route headers. 3) console patch to add resume_vs_new chart. 4) longer-term: add idempotency token header for resume flows and a small server-side window for safe dedupe.

jen: rollback + billing debounce sounds sensible. engineering estimate: rollback 15m, debounce change ~1h dev+canary, console slice 2h.

alexa: do we need legal/billing notifications? finance might want a short note + estimated impact.

mike: initial estimate ~0.08% of daily token volume in EU (non-customer affecting, mostly internal test clients + mobile SDKs). will get a number after quick query.

console-team: can add an emergency filter in Console to isolate events with header `x-resume-attempt:true` so support can slice customers until we ship.

sam: for the debounce implementation pseudo: ```
// billing middleware pseudocode
if event.session_id == previous.event.session_id && time_since(previous) < 500ms && (previous.type == 'new' || current.type == 'resume') then
  coalesce billing into previous_record
else
  emit billing_event
end
```

ryan: watch out for cross-proxy ordering; you need a deterministic key (resume_id) that proxies embed in the route metadata so coalesce can be consistent. otherwise two proxies might both bill.

mike: good call — we should annotate route span with `resume_id` and `proxied_order` and make billing coalesce use resume_id+route_shard as key.

jen: I'll open a PR for the billing debounce and a rollback config change. mike, can you own the console filter?

mike: yep. filing PRs now. also add integration test to simulate resume-before-lease commit.

alexa: once PRs are up, let's do a controlled canary over 10% of EU traffic and monitor resume_vs_new ratio + billing delta. if stable, roll to 100% and then re-enable taproot with a flag guarded rollout.

mike: noted. I'll also add a temporary alert: if resume_vs_new percent > 1.5% spike over baseline -> page oncall.

ops-bot: Action items assigned: mike(rows: console filter, alert), jen(billing debounce PR), sam(long-term idempotency design), console-team(quick UI filter).

ryan: one more UX ask — on the Console billing trace view, surface the 'session lifecycle timeline' so support can see new/resume transitions per session id. small change but big for debugging.

console-team: added to backlog, will try to get into emergency slice if we hit customer tickets.

mike: thanks all — rolling rollback now and will post status in 10m.

jen: thanks, keep us posted. :thumbsup:
